correctness.rationale: For θ=π∘reverse with f≥1 fixed letters and d≥1 transposition pairs, every symmetric word is Hθ(H) or Hcθ(H) for c fixed. The unique greedy arch decomposition of H gives t complete arches and proper-support S, with full word index exactly 2t or 2t+1 according to whether support(S)∪π(support(S)) (plus c for odd words) covers the alphabet. I verified the exact-support surjection series B_j(y), the independent S support sums R,E,O for each allowed number of doubled transposition pairs, and the geometric arch factor 1/(1−u²A(z²)). This yields the displayed bivariate formal GF. Its lowest-degree odd/even coefficients give minimum lengths L_2m=2mq and L_(2m+1)=(2m+1)q+f−1 and multiplicities (q!)^m and (q!)^m f2^d(f+d−1)!; no inference from finite word lengths is needed.
residual_risks: The symmetric midpoint arch lemma is related to established scattered-factor universality theory, so its original status is not asserted.

value.rationale: Mixed involutions (both fixed and paired letters) occur naturally in formal word symmetries and differ sharply from the known all-fixed and all-paired endpoint types. The exact length-by-universality-index rational GF and shortest witness multiplicities answer a complete natural enumeration question, with nontrivial parity and support-covering interactions; these data can be used without needing a further general theorem.
residual_risks: This is not a claim for cyclic/unlabeled words or physical nucleic-acid sequence properties.

limitations: Both fixed and transposed letter orbits are mandatory (f,d≥1); labeled indexed linear words only.
The broad palindrome arch and midpoint logic are prior work, limiting the assessed originality to mixed-type coefficient evaluation.
